sentences.text: The appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the Judgment and Award dated 06.01.2012 passed in MVC No.8669/2010 by the Member, MACT and IV Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore city, for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the case:
On 03.07.2010 at about 9.15 a.m., when the claimant was crossing the road near K.H.Junction, Bengaluru, motor-cycle bearing No.KA-40-L-144 owned and ridden by Respondent No.1 and insured by Respondent No.2 came in high speed and dashed him.
As a result, claimant sustained grievous injuries and was taken to Bowring Hospital, Bangalore and was treated as an inpatient.

The claim petition filed by the claimant was NC: 2023:KHC:21504 partly allowed holding that Respondent No.1-owner and Respondent No.2-Insurance Company were jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

3. Heard arguments of learned counsel for both the parties and perused the records.
4.
In the present case, from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had sustained fracture of tibia and fibula of left leg lower 1/3rd and other grievous injuries all over the body.

5. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:

sentences.text: The claimant had undergone surgery for two times and implants were fixed.
The claimant is an Agricultural Coolie by profession.
Therefore, the compensation amount awarded under the head injuries, pain and suffering is on the lower side.
Hence, the compensation of Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards, injuries, pain and suffering.
The compensation of Rs.5,000/- awarded under the head medical expenses is as per the medical bills produced by the claimant.

7. Further, a compensation of Rs.28,000/- was awarded for incidental expenses like food,
nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance etc.
Same is just and proper.

Since the claimant had undergone surgery for two times by admitting into hospital for two times and the claimant is needed one more surgery for removal of the implants and the screws, the compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.
The Tribunal has held the notional income of Rs.3,000/- p.m., only.
But the accident has occurred in 2010.
Hence, the notional income of Rs.5,500/- p.m., is considered as NC: 2023:KHC:21504 per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The doctor had stated that the claimant had suffered 30.1% of disability towards left lower limb and suffered 20% of disability to the whole body as per doctor's evidence.
Further, the claimant is an Agriculturist by profession.
But the Tribunal has awarded compensation on a meager side.
Hence, the same is required to be enhanced.
Therefore, towards loss of future income, additional compensation has to be added as per the Judgment of this Court in New India Assurance Company Ltd., Vs. Abdul & Others1.

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the case of injury suffered like in the present case, additional income has to be added.

The multiplier applicable is 13.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is re- assessed and quantified as follows:

sentences.text:
Further, for a period of four months, the claimant must not have been in a position to work as an agricultural coolie and lost his income for a period of four months,
which comes to Rs.22,000/- (Rs.5,500/- x 4 months).

Hence, a sum of Rs.22,000/-
is awarded towards loss of earning during laid up period.
Further, a compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
Pain & sufferings Rs.40,000/-
Medical expenses,
Conveyance & Nourishment Rs.5,000/-
Food, nourishment, Attendant Charges and conveyance Rs.28,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up period Rs.22,000/-
Loss of future income on account of Permanent Disability Rs.2,14,500/-
Loss of Amenities Rs.25,000/-
Future Medical Expenses. Rs.25,000/-
 Rs.3,59,500/-
8.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award dated 06.01.2012 passed in MVC No.8669/2010 by the Member, MACT and IV Addl.

Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore city, is modified to an extent that the appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.2,30,700/- (Rs.3,59,500/- -
Rs.1,28,800/-) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court.
v. Draw award accordingly.
